mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above 4% signals a shift to tighter policy, which reduces near-term discounting of equity cash flows, causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in a consecutive month
regime_hint: FED Funds rate above 4% in tightening phase
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat during the trigger, with p-value > 0.05 in a backtest.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS (employment) above 145,000 suggests labor market strengthening, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 145,000 in a month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or insignificant (t-test p > 0.05) during the labor expansion phase.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in HOUST (retail sales) of more than 5% indicates weakening consumer demand, which elevates risk premia and produces negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls >5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive or not statistically different from baseline during the demand contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in INDPRO (industrial production) index below 104 suggests supply-side weakness, raising uncertainty and pushing S&P 500 20-day forward returns to the downside.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 104 in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or not significantly different from baseline during the supply contraction.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) rises above 5%, it reflects labor market tightness that can trigger a risk-off reaction, producing negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 5% in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or not statistically significant in high-unemployment periods.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) above their prior month's levels indicate accelerating economic momentum, which is associated with positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and RSAFS both rise from previous month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or flat despite both proxies rising.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 4% combined with a rise in PAYEMS above 145,000 signals a transition from slack to expansion, which can drive positive S&P 500 20-day returns in early expansion phases.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS > 145,000 in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative during the regime, or UNRATE does not fall below 4% while PAYEMS does not rise above 145,000.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL (CPI) prints a monthly increase above 2% in a tightening environment, it amplifies inflation expectations and produces negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 2% in a month during a tightening regime
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive or not significantly different from baseline during the CPI acceleration.
